  "text": "Every Thursday, someone left a pear on the windowsill beside the building’s broken lift.

Nina noticed because she took the stairs slowly now. On the third-floor landing she stopped to rest her knee, and there it would be: green, yellow, once wrapped in a square of newspaper.

She assumed it belonged to the woman in 3B, who received grocery deliveries and never quite closed her door.

One Thursday, Nina found a banana instead.

“Supply problems,” said a voice behind her.

The caretaker stood on the stairs holding a dustpan.

“Are these yours?” she asked.

“My lunch. I put it down to unlock the cupboard, then forget it.”

“Every week?”

“I only do this building Thursdays.”

She picked up the banana and handed it to him. He tucked it into his shirt pocket, where it stuck out like a ridiculous pen.

The following Thursday, the windowsill was empty. Nina rested beside it anyway.

The caretaker came up carrying a small wooden stool.

“Found this in the basement,” he said. “Thought it might be useful here.”

He set it against the wall without looking at her knee.

She sat while he searched his keys for the cupboard key.

“My husband used to oil our locks,” she said. “I don’t know what he used.”

“Graphite’s best. Oil collects dirt.”

“Oh.”

He opened the cupboard.

“I could have a look next week.”

That Thursday, Nina brought two pears downstairs in a paper bag.

She put one on the windowsill and kept the other in her lap, sitting on the stool until she heard his dustpan knock against the banister."
